name: Debonaire Skin
name_note: Booksy listing still shows the old name 'Debonaire Headspa', but the business's own logo/branding (assets/raw/bk-1.jpg, bk-2.jpg) and Instagram handle clearly say 'Debonaire Skin · Facials & Skin Care'. The full service menu is 100% facial/peeling/skincare, no scalp or head-spa services at all. Site built and named as the real current brand: Debonaire Skin.
owner_source: Booksy staff list shows a single staff member named 'Debonaire Lindsay' (business name + first name pattern used by solo Booksy providers). No last name published.
address_note: No street address published on Booksy (only city + zip, typical of a private/home studio). Reviews mention the esthetician 'set up her equipment in minutes', consistent with a private-suite or mobile setup that shares the exact address only after booking is confirmed. Site copy reflects this honestly instead of inventing a street address.
rating_source: Booksy JSON-LD aggregateRating (ratingValue 5.0, reviewCount 10) on the business's Booksy listing.
language_source: All Booksy reviews are in English; Booksy dossier language heuristic also returned 'en'.
has_own_site_check: debonaireskin.com resolves (HTTP 200) but is a Squarespace 'Coming Soon' parking page with zero real content (3138 bytes, no mailto, no menu, no photos: same pattern as the documented jarelisayala.com precedent). debonaireheadspa.com/.net do not resolve. The only other same_as link on Booksy is https://debonaireskin.etsy.com, an Etsy shop subdomain (third-party marketplace platform, not a self-hosted website, per pipeline rule that platform subdomains do not count). Verdict: no functioning website of their own.
email_source: Searched: Instagram bio (no email, no linktree/external booking link beyond Booksy widget), Booksy dossier payload (phone/email fields both null), debonaireskin.com Coming Soon page (no mailto, no contact info of any kind), no public Facebook page found under this name in Oakland Park/Fort Lauderdale. No email found after exhausting available sources.
services_excluded_note: Booksy also listed 5 offer entries named after individual clients (Ella B, Ashley B.C, Laurel R, Monica C, Sonia White) with their own prices/durations. Verified in the raw Booksy JSON-LD that these are personalized per-client rebooking slots (custom pricing tied to a specific repeat client), not real generic services offered to new customers, so they were excluded from the site's service menu. Only the 6 genuinely generic, publicly bookable facial services above were used.

photo_curation_notes: Reviewed output/debonaireskin/_sheet.jpg (16 photos) one by one. Used clean, real treatment photos (no text/graphics/selfies): bk-13, bk-16, bk-3, bk-7, bk-14 (green sea-spicule mask), bk-5 (male client) and bk-15 (extraction closeup) = 7 usable photos, reused bk-13 and bk-16 once each across hero/experience/gallery to fill all site slots (same accepted pattern as the lashbloom/pureartistry exemplars, which also reuse one photo across two sections). DISCARDED as unusable: bk-1/bk-2 (brand logo graphics, used instead as the small nav/footer/favicon avatar, not gallery tiles), bk-10/bk-12/bk-4/bk-6 (before/after composites with large BEFORE/AFTER text and annotation arrows burned into the image, prohibited by the no-text-overlay gallery rule), bk-8 (chemical-peel-vs-spicule-peel comparison infographic, all text), bk-9 (unrelated 'Cherry' financing-app ad graphic). IG rescue (.venv-pw/bin/python scripts/ig_photos.py _debonaireskin) was attempted for extra variety but returned 0 photos (IG served an empty page to the fetch IP), so the build proceeded with the 7 clean Booksy photos.
palette: Custom navy + terracotta rose-gold palette derived from the business's own logo (navy background, white wordmark/floral line art, assets/raw/bk-1.jpg): --bg #0b1330 (deep navy, matches the real logo bg), --bg-2 #111c44, --ink #f4ece0 (warm cream), --accent-deep #c9895d (terracotta rose-gold), --accent-mid #a8683f, --accent-soft #1a2452. Not one of the 5 DESIGN.md preset palettes and not a repeat of any palette already used in Fort Lauderdale/Oakland Park builds (etherealeyelashesfl: warm gold/ivory light; adryansbarber: dark teal). Merktop badge kept its original gold per pipeline rule.
template_base: templates/dark-v2/index.html (pureartistry exemplar), derived via anchored Python replacements (script kept in scratchpad, not committed).
